metadata.note: The Flying Yankee streamliner, the best-known historical passenger service over the Boston-Portland corridor now served by Amtrak's Downeaster. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.

segments.note: The Flying Yankee, a Budd-built diesel-electric streamliner delivered in 1935 for the B&M and Maine Central, was the third streamliner in North America after Union Pacific's M-10000 and the CB&Q's Pioneer Zephyr. It ran a 750-mile daily cycle: Portland-Boston-Portland-Bangor-Portland-Boston-Portland, covering many of the same stops Amtrak's Downeaster serves today (this geometry shows the Boston-Portland-Brunswick portion; the train continued beyond to Bangor). Retired from passenger service in 1957 and donated to the Edaville Railroad. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
